scope: OCR reference audit of eight 300-DPI grayscale rasterizations from four distinct original EUR-Lex regulations; no OCR model output was used.
source_independence: HTML is an independently retrieved representation of the same official publisher's text. It is not an independent human transcription, a second publisher, or proof that PDF and HTML have no common-source errors.
method: Inspected all eight complete raster images at original resolution using view_image.

Read each complete PDF-text candidate and compared every visible block and its sequence, including running headers, footer identifiers, page-boundary fragments, in-body footnote callouts, and full notes.

For FR, EL, and ES, compared every body block against the corresponding official HTML text retrieved separately. Audit-only normalization was NFC, removal of U+00AD plus its following whitespace to reconstruct the HTML word, removal of Markdown table bars/emphasis characters, and removal of Unicode whitespace. Case, remaining punctuation, digits, and letters were retained.
German official HTML was inspected at corresponding recital anchors; no complete automated body-match claim is made.
Counted Unicode Letter characters after NFC for language-share metadata; this is a reference audit count, not an OCR error score.
limitations: This is an AI-assisted visual and source-alignment audit, not certified native-speaker proofreading or independently authored human gold.
Complete independent HTML footnote checks and local raw HTML hashes were not completed by this subagent; the parent is acquiring those exact files with Rust.
No engine predictions, execution timings, CER/WER measurements, or model accuracy claims were produced.
The eight pages are four document clusters, not eight independent works; each pair shares its source act and publisher layout.
These are clean modern printed legal texts, including regulations discussing health. They are not clinical notes, handwritten legal files, degraded scans, or laboratory records.
Source typographic ambiguities and any grammatical errors remain visible in the audit; do not silently editorially correct them.

rights.scope: Legal documents published in EUR-Lex may be reused commercially or noncommercially unless a document states special conditions. The inspected pages are legislative prose and official citations; no third-party illustrations or identifiable private individuals appear.
rights.cc_by_distinction: The page separately grants CC BY 4.0 to EU-owned editorial website content, legislative summaries, and consolidated texts. Do not label these original Official Journal regulation PDFs CC BY 4.0 merely by transferring that separate grant.
rights.attribution: European Union, Official Journal of the European Union; cite each regulation/CELEX identifier, publication language, original page, source URL, and retrieval/hash lock.
rights.changes: Disclose rasterization and the listed reference-character overlays. Retain original PDFs and candidate extractions. Predictions and evaluation references are derivatives and are not authentic Official Journal documents.
